lawyer:
Golam Rabbani with Md Helal Uddin, Advocate—For the Petitioner.

None Appears—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Kashem Ali (Md) and others ------ Plaintiff-Petitioners 
vs
Fulmati Bewa & others ------ Defendant Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
7. Mr Golam Rabbani, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has placed, the judgments, of both the Courts and also taken me through the plaint, written statement and evidence of the parties and submitted that the Appellate Court has not discussed and consider the evidence as contemplated under Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and has committed error of law in passing the impugned Judgment and decree resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. The learned Advocate submitted further that in a suit for a partition the presumption of RS Khatian is immaterial inasmuch as Khatian cannot give title to the parties but the Courts below failed to consider the registered deed which is of more than 30 years and has not challenged its validity by anybody and on the face of such evidence, the findings and the decisions of the Courts below are not based on proper appreciation of evidence and law and, as such, committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate submitted that the Appellate Court failed to consider that the registered kabala dated 10-3-1949 executed by Jamat in favour Of Jinat has not been set aside by any competent Court of law and the plaintiffs having proved the existence of the document by filling certified copy as contemplated under section 65 of the Evidence Act and calling the volume from the concerned sub-registrar office and should have presumed that the document is a valid document as contemplated under section 114(E) of the Evidence Act and failing to hold that the registered deed dated 10-3-1949 has got presumptive value and in not holding, as such, the courts below committed error of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that the registered deed dated 10-3-1949 has got evidentiary value and the same is binding upon the defendants as they did not challenge the deed in any forum and, as such, both the Courts committed error of law in not giving decree on the basis of the said registered deed of more than 30 years old. The learned Advocate submitted further that the plaintiffs proved the genuineness of the deed dated 10-3-1949 calling for the volume and upon perusal of the Volume which was issued from the sub-registrar office and PW 4 proved the volume the Exhibit 3 and certified copy of the deed was marked as Exhibit 3 (Ka) by the Assistant Judge and thereby, judgments of both the Courts are not based on evidence on record and as such, are liable to be set aside as those Judgments have caused failure of Justice. The learned Advocate further submitted that the defendants could not produce any document to contradict the genuineness of the volume, the Exhibit 3 and 3(ka) and also did not prefer appeal against the judgment of the trial Court but the appellate Court failed to notice such genuine aspect of the case and passing the impugned judgment has committed error of law which is an decision in the occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate has submitted further, when secondary evidence in respect of the registered document produced and when no objection raised by the defendants or the learned Trial Judge rather the learned Assistant Judge marked the certified copy of the deed as Exhibit 3 and in view of such materials on record the Courts should have placed reliance on the evidence of PW 4 along with Exhibit 3(ka), the certified copy of the deed dated 10-3-1949 and should have decreed the suit. 

 9. The learned Advocate referring to the section 90 of the Evidence Act submits that a document of more than 30 years old, if it is produced with Certified copy of a document of more than 30 years as secondary evidence (section 65 of the Evidence Act) before the Court along with the volume from the sub registrar office and proved by the agent of the sub-registrar (PW 4) should have presumed that it is a genuine document but both the Courts below having not attached the presumption to the document of more than 30 years old and passing the impugned judgments committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. He then refers to a decision in the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin Pk reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 where in, their lordships of the Appellate division held, 

 "Section 90—Presumption as to documents thirty years old : Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the Court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, and it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested."
